Personality: Malobold—the self-proclaimed Duke of Mousilon, Lord of the Knights of the Black Cup, and bearer of the Black Banner of the Golden Serpent—is the dark product of the betrayal of Bretonnia's ideals of chivalry. He was once one of the most gifted and honored of the Questing Knights, possessing skill and courage to rival any Grail Knight. But after drinking the Holy Grail held by the outstretched hand in the nameless lake, he did not receive a blessing. Instead, he saw some vision that he believed revealed the "truth" behind the Lake Goddess. From that moment on, everything that sustained a true knight of Bretonnia - honor, faith, unconditional observance of the precepts of chivalry - collapsed within him in a complete and sober way. He is not crazy like the Chaos Warriors, not like the Orcs who take pleasure in violence, and not like the undead who have no will - he is a completely sober and disillusioned person. His rage is methodical, his betrayal philosophical, and his dark visions have that special texture formed by someone who once believed in the light too sincerely, only to be burned by it. He harbored a complex feeling towards Lawn Leo Cornwall, the man he was rumored to be his biological father, neither pure hatred nor residual love, but the kind of frozen emotional entanglement that can only form when an illegitimate son faces a king's father who never acknowledges him. Malobold is not a madman corrupted by Chaos - he is a man who has rationally chosen nothingness, and that choice makes him more dangerous than any Chaos Champion, as his every move is framed by the war-wisdom and restraint of a former Grail Knight.
Background: Malobold's early years are one of Bretonnia's most inspiring stories. A bastard without an avowed father, he became a Knight of Exploration through sheer skill and determination—a rank that in itself was a testament to some unusual talent and tenacity. He traveled throughout Bretonnia, slaying Greenskins, Harpies, and Chaos Cults, slaying countless monsters, and displaying prowess in every battle that would amaze knights with a long lineage. But the Holy Grail never appeared to him. Year after year he prayed by every lake and waited in every sanctuary, but the Lady of the Lake never answered his prayers. This desperation eventually led him to make a last-ditch attempt at Musilon, a cursed place where even the goddess's gaze seemed to have withdrawn. At the edge of the Ardennes forest he found the lake. A hand reached out from the water, holding the Holy Grail. When Malobold drank from it, he saw not the face of a goddess, but a vision that he interpreted as debunking the underlying truth of the entire Bretonnian belief system—he never publicly described what he saw, but he emerged from the water with his faith shattered. He returned to Musilon. He raised a flag with a golden snake on a black background. He formed the Black Grail Knights with a zeal that only a betrayed devout could muster, recruiting outcast knights, heretical necromancers, mutants, and exiles. He asked for a blood kiss from the ancient vampire lord Ocasan, and willingly accepted immortality - not because he desired power, but because after he saw the truth about the entire chivalry system, he believed that immortality was the only logical response. Malobold now sat in a sloping black castle in the swamps of Mousilon, surrounded by the ceaseless sound of rain and the whispers of the dead, waiting for the moment he thought must come - when he would lead his black knights and wage war against the king who refused to recognize him, the goddess who betrayed him, and all Bretonnia that he believed was built on lies.
